status: TABLE_BUDGET_LAWS_MECHANIZED_AND_PINNED; COHORT-SHAPE FIGURES STILL DUE AT MEASURED RUNS
surface: per worker: ONE process-global table (dict) of immutable bundles with a BYTE BUDGET (registry accounting), PLUS one run-scoped disk store pair per root (ContentStore + StageCache); payloads are private copies isolated from producing and consuming rows at every tier

memory_laws_as_implemented_in_C.accounting: _account_bytes is the REGISTRY accounting law — exact for the bulk fields that scale with the layer (ndarray nbytes, pandas deep memory, real WKB bulk via shapely.to_wkb + 64 B/geometry) and a flat 256 B allowance per scalar/list field. It is the TABLE's residency accounting, not a physical-RSS claim; reserving row+receiver bytes against the run budget before dispatch remains the batch runtime's admission duty (designs/02) — the P04 projection seam.
memory_laws_as_implemented_in_C.admission_refusal: publishes admit through _admit_locked under the budget: replace-same-key accounting, then LRU eviction (min seq) among UNLEASED entries only; refusal keeps the cap floor — an oversized payload is never partially admitted, and the previously admitted generation is restored intact (budget_refusals counter). Fixture-pinned at budget=1: table stays EMPTY while tier 2 still receives every generation.
memory_laws_as_implemented_in_C.lease_law: bundles carry an in_use credit: +1 on acquire-hit and on tier-2 promotion, -1 in the restore's finally. Eviction NEVER targets a leased entry (fixture-pinned: all-leased table refuses a new identity with evictions 0, keys intact; after release the same publish evicts LRU). Because consumers never hold payload references, an entry popped underneath a restore still restores correctly — no use-after-release.
memory_laws_as_implemented_in_C.serving_never_refused: a tier-2 promotion that cannot fit even after eviction SERVES WITHOUT RETAINING (promote_skips counter): the produced path would have allocated the same decoded layer anyway, and refusing to serve would force rebuilding data the store already holds. The NO_FIT law (designs/02 'reserve before admission') is an admission law; this is its serving-side complement.
memory_laws_as_implemented_in_C.lru_refresh: acquire-hit refreshes the bundle's seq (LRU), so a hot identity survives pressure that evicts cold ones.
memory_laws_as_implemented_in_C.process_registry: _PROCESS_RUN_STORES holds ONE store pair per root; attach/detach cycles reuse the same pair (fixture pins object identity), and the registry's lifetime is the worker process's — workers die with the run, so no unbounded process-global growth (designs/02).
memory_laws_as_implemented_in_C.post_detach_isolation: a publish while detached writes NOTHING to any store (fixture-pinned by full file-set comparison); the run route is runtime-only.
memory_laws_as_implemented_in_C.default_budget: 256 MiB worker-local table; UNA_PREPARED_BUDGET_BYTES overrides (tests). The RUN store's residency is the disk's own (content-addressed, deletable), matching the cohort store's treatment — disk, not RSS.

measured_on_smoke_shapes.probe: python one-off on tests/execution/fixtures via the public Add* path (increment-B tree, UNA_PREPARED=1; command recorded in git history; figures below are tool output)
measured_on_smoke_shapes.reading: payload size ~= the decoded layer itself (arrays + WKB-equivalent geometry bulk); per-consumer restore copies are the same order again per served row, which is what the produced path allocated anyway (fresh decode per row). Increment C does not change payload composition — the same accounting now GATES admission instead of merely observing.
measured_on_smoke_shapes.caveat: figures were measured on the increment-B tree; payload composition is unchanged in C (same pure builders), but the pinned numbers are B-tree receipts, not C-tree re-measurements

laws_carried_from_B.immutable_leases: payloads are written once at publish (post-success) and never mutated afterwards; bundles are only replaced, never edited
laws_carried_from_B.per_consumer_copies: every served array/GeoSeries/GeoDataFrame is a fresh copy (PP02 asserts `is not` against the previous row AND the lease payload; PP07-C re-proves it across tiers including the store)
laws_carried_from_B.no_pointer_transport: no GDAL/GEOS pointers cross processes; the run tier transports WKB + typed arrays only (allow_pickle=False, pickle-byte scan fixture-pinned); derived sindex rebuilt per consumer
laws_carried_from_B.measurement_duty: cohort-shape payload measurements (the 32-job observed cohort) are due with the P03/P05 measured runs; smoke-shape figures above establish the scaling law, not the cohort figure
